key_insight: The paper gives provably efficient classical and quantum algorithms for finding the Slater determinant that best matches an arbitrary fermionic state, with guarantees near the optimal fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, interpretable baseline for quantum simulation and fermionic state compression, with potential use in Hartree-Fock initialization, tomography, and benchmarking many-body models.
method: Classical and quantum optimization procedures search over Slater determinants to maximize fidelity to an input n-fermion state.
The algorithms achieve fidelity within ε of optimal in time m^poly(n,1/ε), and with quantum copies use poly(m,n,1/ε) copies of ρ.
The paper also analyzes landscape structure, showing a 2/3 fidelity threshold separating benign and spurious stationary points.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports provable performance guarantees, matching hardness lower bounds under standard conjectures, and an application extracting the closest Slater determinant from Fermi-Hubbard neural quantum state solutions.
watch_item: The favorable guarantees depend on polynomial factors in n and 1/ε, so scaling may still be challenging for large fermion number or high precision.
